Behaviors recorded in v2 (README at pinned commit): (1) opt-in anonymous telemetry: asks once on the first setup command (roost, fly, add, service install) in a terminal; nothing sent unless telemetry_enabled = true; endpoint counters sampled once a minute and pushed to iroh-services (relay usage, hole-punching success, bytes moved); the sending endpoint ID is visible to the collector; (2) `pigeons service install` installs a system service (systemd, launchd, Windows SCM) and the roost then runs as root, reading a machine-wide config (/etc/pigeons/config.toml or C:\ProgramData\pigeons\config.toml); (3) `pigeons add` writes a Host entry to ~/.ssh/config (README example output: "Pigeon route 'my-server' added to ~/.ssh/config"); (4) a dedicated keypair .ssh/pigeons_ed25519 is used; (5) security model: anyone holding the endpoint ID can reach the SSH port. M00 fixture rule (inference from CLAUDE.md boundaries): run with HOME pointed at a scratch directory, never run `service install`, and answer or preset telemetry off.

escalations.summary: Suggested spec clarification, not a contradiction. Spec line 323 says remembered approvals do not keep private keys available after lock; S06 and S07 support that as written (unlock still required for key access). S07 also documents timed remembering (4/12/24 h) under which key APPROVALS stay in agent memory while 1Password is locked. A clarifying sentence distinguishing approvals from key availability would prevent misreading; wording is the spec owner's decision.
Spec says ssh -G evaluation may run Match exec; no single source sentence states this; it is an inference. Needs G07/G09 behavioral evidence, not a doc citation.
Bubble Tea v2 module path is charm.land/bubbletea/v2; any plan text assuming github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea import path would be stale.

S22: Iroh JS bindings publish no macOS Intel (darwin-x64) binary; the Rust crate lists macOS x86_64. TS+Iroh on Intel Macs would need a source build. OpenTUI @opentui/core package.json lists engines bun >=1.3.0 and node >=26.4.0 as separate keys; whether either runtime alone suffices, and how native code loads under Node, is INFERENCE until tested in G02.
OpenAI Evals platform banner: read-only 2026-10-31, shutdown 2026-11-30. Guidance text supports the spec claim; the platform should not be a Heimdall dependency.
